newsitem.title: UK: UK Wool Board to launch own environmental research.
newsitem.headline: UK Wool Board to launch own environmental research.

text.p: The British Wool Marketing Board (BWMB) said it will conduct research into the levels of pesticide residues on fleeces and in processing factory effluent.
The Board has been approached by representatives of the UK wool textile industry to help minimise the amount of sheep pesticides washing through the textile production pipeline.
"It is a complex problem," BWMB chairman Alun Evans said in a statement.

"As producers we need to dip our sheep, but we cannot ignore the fact that the water discharged by the textile industry contains levels of pesticides from OP dips which are unacceptably high to meet legislation and could threaten the environment," he said.
While action has been taken by individual processors "there has been no comprehensive research which has established a definite link between the residues and British Wool", he said.
"If the British textile industry is to have the continued confidence to use our wool we need to address the matter ourselves," he added.
The two-year investigation into pesticide practices and their environmental impact will be led by Trevor Shaw of the International Wool Secretariat.
It will involve controlled tests on various wool types from different locations with no conclusive results expected until the summer of 1998, the Board said.
